how: An invitation supplies a proposer without identifying the eventual builder or establishing that others joined this particular starter.
Calls recruit people to start a Miku mark and later to help add a leek.
A participant answers the repair call with the bare commitment Doing my part.
Members negotiate background colour, kerning, compression and lettering while proposing additional characters and a leek.
Participants report the work restored and check its current condition.
Members request a template, publish a taskbar version and circulate new coordinates.
Members rally against erasure and choose upkeep over growth because a larger image exceeds their available hands.
Members identify an attempted overwrite and later distinguish planned taskbar incorporation from complete erasure.
A participant offers rebuilding help after the neighbour dispute, without evidence that rebuilding occurred.
Participants report taskbar discussions, weigh incorporation against relocation and receive peaceful border requests.
A neighbour reports overwritten artwork and a participant justifies covering it as spreading awareness, without an identified attack call.
Members announce a move into a taskbar icon as a way to preserve Miku, while completion remains uncertain.
Members celebrate a recognizable surviving icon and praise the small workforce that maintained it.
The record combines a protective screenshot during building with retrospective accounts of defence and damage.
Survival and pride are documented, but these passages establish no decision to continue the collective or reuse its image.
Four-tile placing and correcting a mention bot do not identify scripts, spare accounts or automated canvas placement.
A neighbour offers maintenance in exchange for heart restoration and another participant proposes helping nearby defenders.
An alliance offer establishes proposed cooperation without showing reciprocal acceptance or a coalition operating.
The overwrite dispute continues through insults and popularity comparisons before a different participant offers repair.
The proposed taskbar icon is a hosted arrangement whose implementation and protection remain unresolved.
A member points participants toward a canvas megathread without establishing moderator enforcement or posting restrictions.
Objecting to Discord access and preferring the original logo do not explicitly challenge authority to bind the room to an inter-room agreement.
After closure a participant corrects the account of complete taskbar erasure by explaining the intended icon conversion.
The coded invitation establishes a canvas proposal without establishing that the host treated it as an April Fools prank.
A participant explicitly limits expansion because there are too few hands to maintain something larger.
The overwrite dispute supplies local grievances without showing a quarrel carried into the event from before it.
Character proposals and a shrine reference establish fandom imagery without establishing that prior lore or ideology governed collective conduct.
The absence of formal office cannot imply an absence of attempted order when prior consultation in a planning venue is demanded and contested.
No cited explanation connects the overwritten logo to an inherited rivalry or prior tie naming it as a target.
A participant reports discussions with the taskbar team and others refer proposals to the person handling diplomacy.
The opening proposal cannot be connected to the later build through a documented response or participant attribution.
The proposer is visible but the record cannot connect this starter to the later recruitment and repair effort.
A build-to-upkeep order cannot be required when the record introduces the artwork already standing and under erasure.
An upkeep request explicitly refers to simultaneous discussion with the taskbar about the work's future.
The rebuilding offer cannot be attributed to an agreed border when the participant instead explicitly credits personal reconsideration of the neighbour's artist.
The record shows pressure and repeated reversals without identifying whether machine hands followed upkeep.
A participant explicitly takes pride in the small workforce maintaining the image, linking recognition to the reported achievement.
Recording need not follow celebration because a protective screenshot circulates during active upkeep before the later achievement account.
Recording survival does not establish a subsequent decision to preserve the collective or move its work elsewhere.
Judged weakness can prompt a negotiated move proposal while resistance continues, so neither completed relocation nor cessation of fighting follows automatically.
Templates and continuing design disagreement are visible, but the record cannot establish that a template settled the room's design.
The repair call receives a direct bare participation report, supporting this local pair without demonstrating obligations for silent readers.
A maintenance-for-restoration offer is visible without evidence that strained upkeep produced an accepted exchange or delivered assistance.
Proposed reciprocal help and taskbar talks do not establish a border agreement opening a channel that subsequently delivered help.
Recruitment and a justified overwrite coexist without evidence that recruitment produced a call to attack the neighbour.
A rebuilding offer follows an overwrite dispute without an observed attack call and refusal pair.
The OVO dispute and taskbar negotiation concern different counterparties and cannot establish an attack call producing a truce.
A neighbour names the overwrite and the direct answers justify it and contest whose artwork matters.
An alliance proposal during maintenance does not establish that pressure resulted in a coalition defending jointly.
Calls and a later megathread pointer establish neither a flood nor a host rule adopted because of flooding.
Off-platform planning and objections to access cannot establish that a neighbour agreement caused a dispute over who could bind the room.

statement: Contesting access to the planning venue
how: Requiring a separate chat account can become a disputed condition for proposing canvas changes, distinct from authority to make inter-room treaties.
Anticipated overrun can prompt a smaller hosted move before the existing work is erased.
A neighbour dispute can turn toward repair through explicit personal reconsideration rather than through a border settlement or a collective apology.
Sparing neighbours describes only part of the dispute, which includes justifying damage and insulting the overwritten artwork before an individual offers rebuilding help.
Crediting a proposed contributor occurs during an unfinished addition, including explaining attribution to a mention bot.

statement: Carrying the costs of upkeep into the account of achievement
how: Participants explain exhaustion, regret at sleeping and attachment through repeated repair alongside collective pride, rather than only celebrating completion.

statement: Wanting visibility without an observed audience return
how: Damaged lettering matters as a lost opportunity for publicity even when no newcomers or growth are observed.
Regret over a missing pixel does not establish cleanup of a shared preserved copy, although a separate correction of the event account is observed.
